name: NAKANO HAKO
card: Coworking with a private community hall, two minutes from the South Exit of Nakano Station
title: NAKANO HAKO — coworking and a private community hall for the neighbourhood, two minutes from Nakano Station
lead: NAKANO HAKO is on the 2nd floor of the Nakano Southerrace Residence tower, about a two-minute walk from the South Exit of JR Nakano Station and directly connected by a deck. It is made up of PRIVATE BOX, a coworking space for work or study; COMMUNITY BOX, a private community hall for the neighbourhood; and OPEN BOX, where artworks can be displayed. There is a quiet focus lounge, an open lounge where you can talk, and a Refresh Box where you take off your shoes and relax. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Coworking space and private community hall
JR Nakano Station South Exit, about 2 min walk (deck-level 2nd floor)
PRIVATE BOX ¥1,200/hour, up to ¥3,400/day (incl. tax; cashless only)
concept: Connect × expand × weave together
Under the motto “connect × expand × weave together”, NAKANO HAKO offers a learning space for study, work and hobbies. The name HAKO (box) stands for “a place for the individual, a place of your own”.
It aims to be a crossroads where users meet and a core for solving problems. Through its private community hall, it also sets out to support local problem-solving as a place where generations gather.
steps: Coworking for working alone or together
PRIVATE BOX is a coworking space for both people who want to focus alone and people who want to relax as in a café.
It costs ¥1,200 an hour or up to ¥3,400 a day, and monthly membership is ¥33,000 for 30 days.
Seats for silence, seats for talking
SHU CHU LOUNGE has wide table seats and private or semi-private seats divided by partitions. Talking and video calls are not allowed there.
OPEN LOUNGE is a space where you can relax as in a café, talk and hold video calls. The Refresh Box is a shoes-off place to take a break.
A private community hall for the neighbourhood
COMMUNITY BOX is a private community hall where people can share hobbies and interests and meet one another. Group registration is required to use it.
There are four rooms; the largest, COMMUNITY BOX-C, is 72 m² for 20 people. There are also A (11 m², 6 people), B (18 m², 8 people) and D (16 m², 6 people).

word.title: What is a community hall (kominkan)?
body: A facility where local people gather for learning, hobbies and social activities. Most are run by local governments.
NAKANO HAKO, as a private facility, runs its own “private community hall”, opening a place for local gatherings on the same floor as its coworking space.

credits: Nishimatsu Jisho Co., Ltd. (linked as the operator on the official website)

name: xBridge-Yaesu
card: Tokyo Tatemono's start-up support hub in Yaesu
title: xBridge-Yaesu — a hub for people who support start-ups, three minutes from the Yaesu North Exit of Tokyo Station
lead: xBridge-Yaesu, run by Tokyo Tatemono, faces Sakura-dori, a three-minute walk from the Yaesu North Exit of JR Tokyo Station. It is a base for “ecosystem builders” — large companies, VCs and others who support start-ups. By day it is a coworking and office space; by night, an event and community space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Tokyo Station Yaesu North Exit, 3 min walk / Tokyo Metro Nihombashi Station, 3–5 min
¥30,000 per seat per month (including Wi-Fi, printer and meeting rooms)
concept: Not just an office, but a strategic base
The official website presents xBridge-Yaesu as “a new hub created together with the ‘ecosystem builders’ who support start-ups' growth”.

It says the space was designed as a base for start-ups and projects backed by large companies and VCs, where ideas and possibilities cross and grow. One line reads: “This is not just an office, but a strategic base for bringing next-generation innovation into society.”
steps: The entrance faces Sakura-dori, within walking distance of both Tokyo and Nihombashi stations.
Contracts are per seat, with 44 seats in the office space. Internet, printers and other equipment are free to use.
Each seat comes with one locker, and there is a fridge, microwave and water server.
A meeting room and booths, free to book
There is one meeting room for 6 and three booths for web meetings and the like. Both are booked in advance and free to use.
An event and community space at night
In the evening, it is rented out as an event and community space for ¥20,000 per hour, with discounts for tenants. A projector, screen and sound system are available.

word.title: What is an ecosystem builder?
body: A company or organisation that helps build the environment (ecosystem) in which start-ups grow, such as corporate venture capital arms of large companies and VCs.
xBridge-Yaesu is aimed at companies and organisations working as ecosystem builders, and at people seeking to create innovation through start-up support.

name: H¹O Shibuya Jinnan
card: Nomura Real Estate's service office, with two lounges
title: H¹O Shibuya Jinnan — two lounges and a rooftop terrace supervised by parkERs
lead: H¹O Shibuya Jinnan, a service office run by Nomura Real Estate, is in Jinnan, Shibuya, a seven-minute walk from Exit B1 of Shibuya Station on the Tokyo Metro. As well as private offices, it has shared lounges for tenants on the 2nd and 8th floors and a terrace on the roof. Interior design of the lounges and rooftop terrace was supervised by parkERs, the spatial design brand of Park Corporation. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Tokyo Metro Shibuya Station Exit B1, 7 min walk
24 hours (no closing days, except statutory inspection days)
hero_cap: The lounge at H¹O Shibuya Jinnan
concept: Another place to be, outside your private office
H¹O is a service office run by Nomura Real Estate. You can rent a private office with utilities included, and it is designed for start-ups, projects and branch offices.
Shibuya Jinnan offers plenty of shared space outside the private offices: lounges for a change of scene or quick meetings on the 2nd and 8th floors, and a terrace on the roof.
steps: Two lounges, on the 2nd and 8th floors
Shared lounges for a change of scene or quick meetings are on the 2nd and 8th floors.
The interior design of the lounges on floors 1, 2 and 8 and the rooftop terrace was supervised by parkERs.
A salon for many ways of working
The official website presents a “HUMAN FIRST SALON for a wide range of work styles”. There is also a PHONE BOOTH for calls.
On the roof is a green rooftop terrace, described on the official website as “an open space with a panoramic view of Shibuya's streets”.
You can come and go 24 hours a day, with no closing days (except statutory inspection days). The building was completed in August 2020.

word.title: What is a service office?
body: An office where you can rent a private room by the month, with furniture, equipment and reception services included. Shared lounges and meeting rooms are often available.
The lounges at H¹O Shibuya Jinnan are shared facilities for tenants; there is no information on public drop-in use.

credits: Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

Basic design: Nomura Real Estate first-class architects' office / design and construction: Tokyu Construction / interior design supervision: parkERs (Park Corporation; lounges on 1F, 2F, 8F and rooftop terrace)
© Nomura Real Estate (H¹O official website: “H¹O Shibuya Jinnan”)

name: H¹O Toranomon
card: A window-side personal lounge, directly linked to Toranomon Station
title: H¹O Toranomon — a lounge overlooking Kasumigaseki, in a building directly linked to the station
lead: H¹O Toranomon, a service office run by Nomura Real Estate, is in Tokyo Toranomon Global Square, directly linked to Toranomon Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, one minute on foot. It stands out for the Connective Lounge, exclusively for tenant companies, and the Personal Lounge, with single sofas lined up along floor-to-ceiling windows. Interior design of the 5th-floor lounge and common areas was supervised by Draft. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Directly linked to Tokyo Metro Ginza Line Toranomon Station, 1 min walk
24 hours (no closing days, except statutory inspection days)
concept: A glass lounge opening onto a street corner

The official website describes it as “in the front row of the Toranomon area”. The building was developed together with Toranomon Station, and a level path leads from the ticket gates to the B1 entrance.
Making use of a site with corners on all four sides, it was designed with floor-to-ceiling glass and 3,000 mm ceilings for an open feel — the highest ceiling height in the H¹O series.
steps: A shared lounge exclusively for tenant companies, usable for meetings, light meals and more. It can also host meetings with visitors and events.
Single sofas line the floor-to-ceiling windows, with a panoramic view over the Kasumigaseki area. The official website describes it as “a refined space inspired by a first-class lounge”.
Corridors with moving images, and six meeting rooms
Projection mapping showing more than ten seasonal animations is used at points along the shared corridors.
There are six meeting rooms, some with camera-equipped displays and AI speakers with 360° cameras.
A shared corridor with projection mapping
The entrance is double-height, with flapper gates. On the 4th floor is a Conference room holding up to 117 people.

word.title: What does “directly linked to the station” mean?
body: You can walk from the station gates or underground passages into the building without going outside.

H¹O Toranomon's building was developed together with Toranomon Station, and the official website notes that thanks to the direct underground passage, you can arrive without an umbrella even on rainy days.

credits: Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.
Nomura Real Estate first-class architects' office / interior design supervision: Draft Inc. (5F lounge and common areas)
© Nomura Real Estate (H¹O official website: “H¹O Toranomon”)

name: H¹O Shibakoen
card: A lounge of wood and greenery, facing Shiba Park
title: H¹O Shibakoen — a lounge of wood and greenery in a hybrid timber building
lead: H¹O Shibakoen, a service office run by Nomura Real Estate, faces Shiba Park, a three-minute walk from Onarimon Station on the Toei Mita Line. Like H¹O Aoyama, it uses a hybrid timber structure as an environmentally considerate office. The lounge uses wood and greenery throughout, with interior design supervised by Line Inc. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Toei Mita Line Onarimon Station, 3 min walk / Shibakoen Station, 4 min / Toei Oedo Line Daimon Station, 4 min
24 hours (no closing days, except statutory inspection days)
concept: A timber office facing Shiba Park
The official website says: “Six lines from four stations. An environmentally considerate service office with a hybrid timber structure, right in front of Shiba Park.”
It is in an area where a town-planning vision centred on Shiba Park has been drawn up, and is presented as a place that carries on the area's culture and history.
steps: A lounge of wood and greenery
The lounge uses wood and greenery throughout, described as a comfortable, relaxing space.
Wi-Fi is available in the shared lounge and meeting rooms.
A rooftop terrace for working outdoors
The rooftop terrace has desks, chairs, power outlets and Wi-Fi, so you can work outdoors. Hours of use are limited.
Meeting rooms and offices in different designs
There are many meeting rooms in different designs, plus private rooms for web meetings.
Every private office has its own air conditioning, and walls that can't be seen through from the shared corridor.

word.title: What is a hybrid timber structure?
body: A building structure that combines wood with other materials, such as steel or reinforced concrete, to support the building.
H¹O Shibakoen is presented as an environmentally friendly office using this structure.

credits: Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.
Design: Nomura Real Estate and Kumagai Gumi first-class architects' offices / construction: Kumagai Gumi / interior design supervision: Line Inc.
© Nomura Real Estate (H¹O official website: “H¹O Shibakoen”)

name: Tatami Works
card: A two-storey workplace with tatami, three minutes from Chitose-Funabashi Station
title: Tatami Works — coworking in tatami rooms, three minutes from Chitose-Funabashi Station
lead: Tatami Works is a coworking space in Funabashi 1-chome, Setagaya, a three-minute walk from Chitose-Funabashi Station on the Odakyu Line. As the name suggests, it is a workplace that incorporates tatami. The ground floor is for conversation, and the 2nd floor for focused work, with both floor seating and chairs. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Odakyu Line Chitose-Funabashi Station, 3 min walk (no parking; 5 bicycle spaces)
24 hours, no closing days (locked 19:00–8:00; membership plan required for those hours)
concept: A place to turn “what if” into reality
Tatami Works is a coworking space whose motto is “a place where you can give shape to your ‘what if’” — somewhere to turn the ideas you picture into real things.

Its facilities page notes that tatami rooms help regulate humidity, and that igusa, the rush used in tatami, is said to have a relaxing effect. It suits remote work, reading and exam study, and is used by a wide range of people including freelancers, homemakers and students.
steps: A relaxed floor where you can talk
The ground floor is a space for working in comfort, with a work area, community space, bookshelves and lockers.
Eating is allowed (nothing strong-smelling or noisy), and Zoom and phone calls are fine.
A focus floor with floor seats or chairs
The 2nd floor is for focused work, with both floor seating and chairs.
You can eat here, but phone calls and Zoom are not allowed.
Free equipment and monthly plans by time of day
Monitors, chargers, mice, keyboards, laptop stands, desk lamps, a whiteboard, a printer and blankets are free to use (limited numbers). Wi-Fi runs on a line of up to 10 Gbps.

Drop-in is ¥500 an hour or ¥2,500 a day. Monthly plans are ¥22,000 for full access, ¥16,500 for weekday daytime, ¥12,100 for nights and ¥8,800 for mornings, and there is an address service usable for company registration (¥5,000 a month).

word.title: What is igusa?
body: A rush plant used to weave the surface of tatami mats, known for its distinctive scent.
Tatami Works highlights working in a tatami room, and mentions that igusa is said to have a relaxing effect.

name: LOUNGE by m Shakujii-koen
card: Work at a wide window-side table, on a 2nd floor in Shakujiimachi
title: LOUNGE by m Shakujii-koen — “a moment of bliss in a refined space”
lead: LOUNGE by m Shakujii-koen is a coworking space on the 2nd floor of Blue Stone in Shakujiimachi 2-chome, Nerima. There are wide window-side tables, individual workspaces and seats that can be closed off with curtains. You enter and leave by tapping an IC card key, and there is a drink bar. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Registration ¥1,650; first hour ¥990, then ¥495 per 30 minutes
Private meeting space ¥550/hour (up to 2 hours, up to 4 people)
concept: A moment of bliss in a refined space
LOUNGE by m has sites in Oizumi-Gakuen and Shakujii-koen in Nerima City. Its official website carries the line “a moment of bliss in a refined space”.
Coworking membership is available at the Shakujii-koen site; the Oizumi-Gakuen site is described as a “learning café”.
steps: A wide window-side table and individual seats
By the windows is a workspace with a wide table, plus individual workspaces. The official website describes the whole site as “a spacious place”.
Draw the curtain to focus or meet
Some seats can be closed off with curtains for focused work, and can also be used for meetings (charged).
The meeting space can be hired for ¥550 an hour, for up to two hours and four people.
IC card entry and a drink bar
Just tap your IC card key to enter and leave; your arrival and departure are recorded automatically.
There are chargers, Wi-Fi, power and a drink bar. Prices are ¥1,650 to register, ¥990 for the first hour and ¥495 per 30 minutes after that.

word.title: What is a drink bar?
body: A self-service station where you pour whatever drinks you like.
LOUNGE by m Shakujii-koen offers a drink bar as one of its workspace amenities.

credits: LOUNGE by m (operating company being confirmed)
© LOUNGE by m (official website: Shakujii-koen photos on the top page)

name: STAYUP Yokohama
card: A 14th floor with views of the Bay Bridge, six minutes from Yokohama Station
title: STAYUP Yokohama — a designer office overlooking Minato Mirai, six minutes from Yokohama Station
lead: STAYUP Yokohama, a coworking space and shared office, is on the 14th floor of Yokohama Creation Square in Sakaecho, Kanagawa Ward, about a six-minute walk from the Kita-Higashi (north-east) Exit of Yokohama Station. On a floor with windows looking out to Minato Mirai and the Bay Bridge are an open space, focus booths, meeting rooms and private rooms. Staff are on hand during the day on weekdays and weekends; at other times it runs unstaffed. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Yokohama Station Kita-Higashi Exit, about 6 min walk (JR, Keikyu, Tokyu Toyoko & Minatomirai lines)
Staffed weekdays 8:30–18:00, weekends 9:00–18:00 (unstaffed at other times)
concept: Stylish × Urban × BusinessLife
STAYUP Yokohama is a designer-office coworking space under the banner “Stylish × Urban × BusinessLife”. Besides Yokohama, STAYUP has sites in Shonan Fujisawa, Saitama Omiya and Hatchobori.

The official website describes it as a “service office” whose mission is to accelerate members' businesses and create synergy between them, and says that in five years since the Yokohama site opened, 26 business connections have been made.
steps: High-performance chairs and a bay view
The open space is furnished with high-performance chairs, and electric sit-stand desks let you work standing up.
From the 14th-floor windows you can see Minato Mirai and the Bay Bridge. Drop-in is ¥880 an hour or ¥2,750 a day.
The view of Minato Mirai and the Bay Bridge
Focus rooms for online meetings, and dedicated offices
There are focus rooms for online meetings and private booths.
Semi-private personal booths start at ¥66,000 a month, and dedicated private offices at ¥132,000 a month.
A focus room for online meetings
Sofa seats for breaks and lunch, and about 30 drinks
Sofa seats screened from view are used for breaks and lunch. There are about 30 kinds of free drinks.
A smart lock lets you enter with Suica or face recognition, and monthly members can print up to 1,000 pages a month free.
The meeting room for 4 (40-inch monitor) is ¥2,200 an hour; the room for 6 (60-inch monitor and whiteboard) is ¥2,750 an hour. Monthly members get ¥550 an hour off.
There is also an event space for seminars of up to 40 people.
A focus room for online meetings

word.title: What is a service office?
body: An office with furniture, internet, reception and other services in place, so you can start working as soon as you sign up.
STAYUP describes itself as a service office that aims to create synergy between members.

credits: STAYUP (listed in the official website footer as a Radix Group site)

name: STAYUP Shonan Fujisawa
card: A spacious floor with greenery, five minutes from the South Exit of Fujisawa Station
title: STAYUP Shonan Fujisawa — a designer space with greenery, five minutes from Fujisawa Station
lead: STAYUP Shonan Fujisawa, a coworking space and shared office, is on the 6th floor of the Mega SanS Building in Kugenuma-Ishigami 1-chome, about a five-minute walk from the South Exit of Fujisawa Station on the JR and Odakyu lines. A designer space with greenery, its floor is described on the official website as one of the largest in Fujisawa. Web meetings are possible at every seat, and there are soundproof booths, meeting rooms and a café space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Tokaido Main Line & Odakyu Enoshima Line Fujisawa Station South Exit, about 5 min walk / Enoshima Electric Railway Fujisawa Station, about 4 min
Staffed weekdays 9:00–18:00 (closed weekends and holidays; monthly 24/365 plan available)
concept: A Shonan designer space with greenery
STAYUP Shonan Fujisawa is a designer coworking space with greenery. Web meetings are possible at every seat, with fast Wi-Fi.
STAYUP has sites in Yokohama, Shonan Fujisawa, Saitama Omiya and Hatchobori. Shonan Fujisawa offers a monthly plan that includes use of the Yokohama site.
steps: Roomy seats where you can hold web meetings
Web meetings are possible at every seat, making it well suited to people working alone. Seats are generously spaced, with plenty of high-performance chairs.
Window seats have monitors and monitor arms.
Booths where you can talk freely
There are soundproof booths for people who want better sound isolation or need to focus. Standing desks are also available.
About 30 drinks and rooms for up to 8
The café space has about 30 kinds of free drinks, plus sofa seats screened from view.
Meeting rooms cost ¥1,650 an hour for 6 people and ¥2,200 an hour for 8. They are reservation-only, and monthly members get ¥550 an hour off.

word.title: What is a soundproof booth?
body: A small enclosed room that keeps your voice in and outside noise out, used for calls and online meetings.
STAYUP Shonan Fujisawa has soundproof booths for people who want better sound isolation or need to focus.

credits: STAYUP (listed in the official website footer as a Radix Group site)
